hints: Look carefully at the words 'in one of the nuclei during telophase'. Sister chromatids have already separated and are now in two separate groups, so focus on what is inside just one new nucleus.
Remember each single chromatid has two ends, so each chromosome present in telophase contributes 2 telomeres. How many chromosomes are in one daughter nucleus after mitosis?
walkthrough:
**Recall what a telomere is**

Think of a chromosome as a little rod with two protective caps, one on each end. Those caps are the telomeres.

So rule to remember:
$$1 \text{ chromatid} = 2 \text{ telomeres}$$

**Work out what is in one nucleus in telophase**

Mitosis makes two identical daughter nuclei. The parent cell started with 38 chromosomes, so after sister chromatids separate in anaphase, each new nucleus in telophase also gets 38 chromosomes.

Crucially, by telophase each chromosome is made of only one chromatid, because the sisters have pulled apart.

**Calculate the total**

Now it is simple multiplication. One nucleus has 38 single-chromatid chromosomes, each with 2 telomeres.
$$38 \times 2 = 76$$
So you will see 76 glowing telomeres in one nucleus.

options.A: 38 would mean only one telomere per chromosome. Every chromatid has two ends, so this misses half the telomeres.
options.B: Correct. One telophase nucleus contains 38 single-chromatid chromosomes, each with 2 telomeres, giving 38 x 2 = 76.
options.C: 114 has no biological basis here. It does not match 2 telomeres per chromosome for 38 chromosomes.
options.D: 152 is 38 x 4. That is the total for duplicated chromosomes with two chromatids in prophase, or for both daughter nuclei combined, not for one nucleus in telophase.
